doc.body:
Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries no endpoint, server lifetime
 or liveness evidence. Render an ID for external text; use its numeric
 accessor when an application needs the mathematical value.

Start with :obj:`parseSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseSessionId>`, :obj:`parseWindowId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseWindowId>` or :obj:`parsePaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:parsePaneId>`. Each type's
 documentation links its parser and renderer. Contextual numeric indices
 belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Value <LibTmux.Value>`.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
Right "@17"
>>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")
"rejected"
```
doc.summary: Distinct session, physical-window and physical-pane IDs.

doc.body:
Construction and access are pure. Window-link indices and pane indices
 have distinct types; neither substitutes for an entity ID. A constructor
 checks the mathematical domain, while command-specific limits belong at
 the operation boundary. Use :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>` and :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`
 to validate input; their accessors return mathematical integers. Entity
 identifiers belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Id <LibTmux.Id>`.



```haskell
>>> fmap dimensionValue (mkDimension 120)
Right 120
>>> mkDimension 0
Left (NonPositiveDimension 0)
```
doc.summary: Positive dimensions and nonnegative contextual indices.

doc.body:
These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute `tmux -V`
 nor contact a server. Admission establishes the minimum release only;
 individual features still need capability and conformance checks.

Use :obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>` for input, :obj:`requireSupported <LibTmux.Version#v:requireSupported>` for minimum-version
 admission and :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>` for canonical output.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3\n" >>= requireSupported)
Right "3.3"
```
doc.summary: Parse stable tmux releases and apply the minimum-version admission check.

A session's unsigned 32-bit tmux identifier, written with a `$` prefix.
 Parse with :obj:`parseSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseSessionId>`; render with :obj:`renderSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:renderSessionId>`.

A physical window's identifier, independent of its session links.
 Parse with :obj:`parseWindowId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseWindowId>`; render with :obj:`renderWindowId <LibTmux.Id#v:renderWindowId>`.

A physical pane's identifier, written with a `%` prefix.
 Parse with :obj:`parsePaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:parsePaneId>`; render with :obj:`renderPaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:renderPaneId>`.

Positive cells, constructed with :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`. Command and field limits
 are checked separately. Compare dimensions directly or use :obj:`dimensionValue <LibTmux.Value#v:dimensionValue>`
 with an integer literal.

 Construct with :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>`; read with :obj:`windowIndexValue <LibTmux.Value#v:windowIndexValue>`.

Nonnegative pane index within a window, not a pane ID.

A stable release, constructed by :obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>` and rendered by
 :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>`. Ordering compares numeric components before the patch letter.
Invalid release syntax or a release below the supported floor.
Bounded copy of input that is not a stable release.
A stable release older than plain tmux 3.3.

Parse a stable release or the output of `tmux -V`, allowing one final LF.
 Development builds and trailing data are rejected rather than assigned
 capabilities from a guessed stable version. Diagnostics retain at most 64 chars.
Render the canonical release without the executable name or newline.

Reject releases older than plain 3.3. Individual features need their own
 capability checks; passing this check does not qualify an entire release.
